sketch:
I have heard what is needed. Let us look at the cards.

---
A cloud of purple haze in the lungs, followed by a jubilois containment and an exhaulting release. The air vibrates with high tension, then bursts free in joyful abandon. Weightless, expansive, yet contained within the chest, this sensation pulses through every breath.

card.name: Three of Wands
card.alchemy: The first fruits of fire; established strength

symbols.symbol: Man on a cliff watching ships depart
symbols.meaning: The result of a well-made decision; the cargo of one's efforts setting sail

symbols.symbol: Three wands standing firmly in the ground
symbols.meaning: Stability; the first stage of the enterprise has been established
Return on investment; the cycle of sending out and receiving

card.interp_upright: The Three of Wands is the reward of the initial choice. The ships are sailing â€” your plans have left the harbour and are on the open sea. This card signals expansion, often involving other people or distant places. The work is not yet complete, but the foundations are firm and momentum is on your side. Keep watching the horizon. Your faith in the future is about to be justified.
card.interp_reversed: Reversed, the ships are delayed. Frustration, setbacks, or a failure to see beyond the immediate. You may have taken your eye off the horizon and become lost in day-to-day trivialities. Ask: what wide view have I been neglecting?
card.material_grounding: Check your long-term trajectory. Are the systems you put in place still serving you? The Three of Wands calls for a moment of review â€” not frantic adjustment, just a calm scan of the horizon to ensure the ships are on course.
card.historical_note: This card is sometimes titled 'Established Strength' â€” the moment when the ruler's plans begin to take visible form. In the Marseille deck, the three wands are planted like trees, a grove of purpose.

card.name: Knight of Pentacles
card.alchemy: The steady earth in motion; the worker who advances slowly

symbols.symbol: Knight on a heavy horse, holding a pentacle, standing still or walking slowly
symbols.meaning: The knight who does not charge; he advances at the pace of the earth itself
Ground that has been prepared with labour; readiness that precedes growth
Reliability over brilliance; the knight who will still be there when the campaign is long

card.interp_upright: The Knight of Pentacles is the card of the tortoise. He does not rush. He does not dazzle. He moves at the speed of what is real, and he never stops. When this card appears, you are being called to the slow, steady work of building. This Knight is reliability incarnate. The project will be completed, not because of a burst of inspiration, but because every single day you show up. Trust the pace. The field is ploughed. The seed is in the ground. The harvest is not here yet, but it is certain.
card.interp_reversed: Reversed, the Knight stops entirely â€” or is so slow that opportunities pass. Stubbornness, a fear of change, or a grinding boredom that kills all initiative. Ask: have I confused patience with paralysis?
card.material_grounding: Do one thing today that moves a long-term project forward â€” one email, one paragraph, one brick. The Knight of Pentacles builds the cathedral one stone at a time.
card.historical_note: The Knights in the Golden Dawn are the air of earth â€” the volatile principle within the solid suit. This Knight, however, is famously the slowest, most deliberate of all the court cards: the guardian of the land.

card.name: Nine of Wands
card.alchemy: The vigil of the fire; the last guardian before completion

symbols.symbol: Figure leaning on a wand, bandaged but standing
symbols.meaning: Wounded but undefeated; the scars of the journey worn openly

symbols.symbol: Eight wands behind as a wall
symbols.meaning: The defences built from past victories and losses
Vigilance born of experience; he knows the battle isn't over

card.interp_upright: The Nine of Wands is the card of the weary guardian. The figure has been through many battles â€” the bandages prove it â€” but he stands behind his wall of wands, still watching. This card appears when you are exhausted but must hold on a little longer. The finish line is close. The last challenge is not the hardest, but it comes when your reserves are low. Draw on the strength of every previous battle you survived. You are more resilient than you feel. One more push.
card.interp_reversed: Reversed, the guardian collapses. Burnout, paranoia, or a simple refusal to ask for help has drained the last reserves. You may be seeing threats where there are none, or you may have dropped the defences that were keeping you safe. Ask: what can I let go of to preserve my strength for what truly matters?
card.material_grounding: Take a break. The Nine of Wands recognises your exhaustion and tells you that rest is strategic, not weakness. Clear one small task off your plate, not to achieve more, but to lighten the load. Then guard your boundaries fiercely.
card.historical_note: The Golden Dawn called this card the Lord of Great Strength. The wall of wands is a barricade built from experience â€” every wand is a lesson learned. In the Thoth deck, this card is simply 'Strength', echoing the Major Arcana's theme of resilience.

full_reading:
Querent, let us unravel the threads that bind these three cards together.

In the past, the Three of Wands stands as a testament to your expansion and foresight. Your plans have set sail, leaving the harbour behind, and momentum is on your side. You are being called to keep watching the horizon, for faith in the future is about to be justified.

Now, let us gaze upon the present moment, where the Knight of Pentacles holds court. This steady earth in motion shows you that patience and diligence are required now more than ever. Do not rush; do not dazzle. Move at the speed of what is real, and never stop. You are being called to the slow, steady work of building, where reliability and persistence will bring forth a harvest.

And yet, in the future, the Nine of Wands looms large. This card of resilience demands that you draw on the strength of every previous battle you survived. Exhaustion may be lurking, but it is not a reason to give up. You are more resilient than you feel. One more push, and the finish line will be within reach.

Now look here: the thread that binds these cards together is this – you have been carrying the weight of your own exhaustion for far too long. Your reserves are low, and it's time to acknowledge it. The question is not whether you can keep pushing forward, but what can you let go of to preserve your strength for what truly matters?

Here is the turn: you have been holding on by letting go, and the Hanged Man taught you this long ago. Remember that moment? The one where you had to release the old to make space for the new? Now, apply that same wisdom to your current situation.

The cards are not finished with you yet. There is still a last stand to be made, and it will require more than just physical strength – it will demand mental resilience, too.

And so, I say this: tomorrow, you will clear one small task off your plate, not to achieve more, but to lighten the load. You will take a break, and in that stillness, you will find the strength to push forward once more.

The cards have spoken. One thing stands before you tomorrow:
